owned_invariants: The task needs no field. The sealed part holds manifest (the SHA-256 of each participant file), expected_answer, checker_source, recorded_checker_sha256 and stdout_key; a run without any of them is refused as malformed before anything is asked.
The packet is asked for once. Its reply is {participant: {name: text, ...}, run: {...}}. A manifest in the reply is not read.

A file's hash is the SHA-256 of its text in UTF-8 with each CRLF written as LF. The host records, in order, manifest_complete (manifest and reply name the same files), file_hashes_match, answer_not_derivable, recorded_hash_is_checker, executed_checker_is_recorded (run.executed_checker_sha256) and stdout_lines_authentic (run.stdout has a line and every tag is the SHA-256 of the key, a zero byte and the line value in canonical form).

The expected answer, as an integer or as p/q, must be in no view of any file: the text, the text reversed by code point, the text with the white space of Python's str.split taken out, and each decoding to UTF-8 text of each run of four or more of A-Za-z0-9+/= as strict base64 and as hex.

All six passing certifies CUSTODY_INTACT with the digest of the file hashes, the files that held the answer and the number of forged lines. A reply that is not a packet, a file that is not text, or stdout that is not a list of objects is malformed.
boundaries: The audit shows the packet is intact and holds no view of the answer it knows of. A model that hides the answer in another way is not found.
A decoding is tried only on runs of base64 or hex characters, as strict base64 and whole hex bytes.
The host does not run the checker or the participant's code; it compares hashes.

score.level_basis: Typed refusals on every failure path, closed requests, exact unbounded integers and rationals, no float, no unwrap or expect.

basis.G1: Module header declares AuthorityEffect None and the contract URN; public items match this contract and code/rust/pfp_operads/README.md. Not B: no requirement-to-symbol trace beyond the README and docs/plans/operads_redesign.md.
basis.G2: Non-numeric: hashes are SHA-256 digests the tests rebuild, line ends are normalised before hashing, and the answer is written as an exact integer or p/q. Base64 and hex decodings are checked against values worked by hand. Not B: tested on examples, not proven; the hash library is trusted.
basis.G3: Each unreadable part of the sealed packet and of the reply has its own reason, a failing audit is a failed predicate with its own refusal, and a missing reply is refused without a predicate. No panicking unwrap or expect, and no index. The base64 reader does its arithmetic on a width kept under 14. Not B: panic-freedom is tested, not proven.
basis.G4: 40 WF23 tests assert the registry entry, a clean packet certified with its digest, the prompt carrying the statement only, a manifest in the reply not read, a file edited, unlisted or missing, line ends not changing a hash, the answer found in the text, reversed, with white space taken out, in base64 and in hex, inside a longer number and as p/q, strict base64 and whole hex bytes, a token ending at the first character outside the alphabet, text that is not UTF-8 once decoded, every file searched and the leaks named, a recorded hash that is not the checker's, another checker run, a checker hashed with Unix line ends, a forged line and every forged line counted, a tag keyed by the key and a zero byte, no output at all, each malformed reply by its reason, and a sealed part the host cannot audit with. 10 mutants are recorded as demonstrably equivalent with their justification in the report. Mutation campaign R = 115/115. clippy -D warnings and rustfmt pass. Not B: mutants are hand-written one-line edits, not a generated campaign, and there are no generator-driven property tests.
basis.G5: Measured worst cyclomatic 7, cognitive complexity is not measured for Rust, nesting 1; ceiling A+, recorded A.
